sections.what_happened: Trump defended the US strikes on Iran, saying 'we blew the hell out of their nuclear capacity, you know that, and far greater than anyone even thought. It's gone,' and arguing Iran would use a nuclear weapon if allowed one. He claimed oil transit through the Strait of Hormuz had surpassed pre-war levels: 'oil coming out of the Strait of Hormuz is now topping what it was before the war' and 'we have more oil coming right now out of the Strait of Hormuz than it was before the war started,' crediting the US naval blockade and Navy. This is a DIFFERENT interview from the Fox News Sunday Morning Futures interview ('finish them off' / 'we now control the Hormuz Strait') recorded totw-20261025-2300-01 / totw-20261026-0200-05.
sections.what_verified: Utterance confirmed by a single wire family (ANI carries agree verbatim on both quotes). PASS rests on the primary-source exception: the primary source is Trump's own on-camera FOX 2 Detroit interview itself, reported by ANI; the record publishes the statement as a PRIMARY-SOURCE CLAIM only. Underlying facts contested: no IAEA or other independent verification of total nuclear-capacity destruction was retrieved; the 'topping pre-war' oil claim is contradicted by the freshest counted maritime data (UKMTO/JMIC, below) and only partly supported by Kpler (crude exports reached pre-war levels in September, at least 16.5 million barrels/day excluding Iran -- 'reached', not 'topped', and September, not now).
sections.what_disputed: UKMTO/JMIC Advisory Note Oct 25 (via Shafaq, recorded totw-20261026-0100-01): 101 vessels transited Hormuz Oct 22-24 vs an average of about 138 vessels per day in 2025 -- 'severely disrupted', not above pre-war. IMF PortWatch backbone: newest snapshot remains portwatch-2026-10-24.json, stale=true, latest observation 2026-10-18: Hormuz counted 4 transits that day, 7-day average 3.71 vs 2025 baseline 85.53/day -- cited ONLY with its Oct 18 observation date and stale flag; PortWatch (AIS transit-call count) and UKMTO (72h vessel transits) count differently and are not reconciled here. Kpler (T3, via Manila Times Oct 25): crude exports reached pre-war levels in September, at least 16.5mbd excluding Iran. No claimant figure is presented as a counted figure.
sections.why_matters: Two claims, one check: Trump's own words say Hormuz oil is beating pre-war levels -- the counters say the strait is still 'severely disrupted'. Put the quote and the UKMTO count side by side; do not repeat the nuclear-destruction claim as fact.
sections.context: Background: MISSED CATCH-UP (in no prior scan) -- Trump FOX 2 Michigan interview: US strikes 'blew the hell out of' Iran's nuclear capacity; Hormuz oil transit now 'topping' pre-war levels

totw_analysis: Our read: Two claims, one check: Trump's own words say Hormuz oil is beating pre-war levels -- the counters say the strait is still 'severely disrupted'. Put the quote and the UKMTO count side by side; do not repeat the nuclear-destruction claim as fact. The fault line our audience is arguing over: Trump's 'more oil than before the war' claim vs what people pay at the pump and what maritime counters actually count -- the White House's own Oct 22 Iran post drew 17K likes / 7.1K comments, dominated by scepticism ('If so much oil is coming thru than why are we paying record high prices?') and dispute over the protester death toll.
